summary.text: 那 commonly means “that” or “those.” Its spelling is linked to 𨙻, which a Shuowen entry describes as the name of a western state. Whether that state-name use came before the demonstrative remains disputed; borrowing based on similar sound has been proposed.

formation.text: The traditional phonosemantic analysis applies to 𨙻: 邑 marks a city or place category, while 冄 is assigned a sound role. The graph is identified as a variant spelling of 那, but the available account does not establish a dated sequence connecting their forms or meanings.

components.text: In the analysis of 𨙻, 邑 contributes the city or place category. This component account applies to that graph, rather than establishing a breakdown for every form or use of 那.
In 𨙻, 冄 is assigned a sound role and is identified as a variant of 冉. The proposed hanging-hair depiction for 冉 is uncertain.

sound_limitation.text: Modern Mandarin readings offer a comparison, but do not establish the ancient sound relation. Zhengzhang reconstructions use differing rhyme notation for 那 and 冉, and no paired Baxter–Sagart reconstruction for 冉 is supplied.

sound.text: In modern Mandarin, 冄 is rǎn and 𨙻 is nà. These readings do not prove the historical sound relation.

history.text: The Shuowen analysis is recorded under 𨙻. A dictionary identifies that graph as a variant spelling of 那 and reports that it was shortened to 那; the account does not provide dated stages for this change. A seal-script form is associated with the Shuowen entry, but is not specifically identified as 𨙻.

Modern 那 is reported absent from oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions, and it is not the form quoted in the Shuowen entry. In 𨙻, 冄 is identified as a variant of 冉; the precise graphic sequence is not established.

uncertainties.text: Accounts differ on whether the earliest sense associated with the spellings was a state name or a distal demonstrative. Their graphic relationship does not settle the word’s origin.
The traditional analysis assigns 冄 a phonetic role in 𨙻, but the available reconstruction comparisons do not independently demonstrate that relationship.

senses.period: Tang poem cited; exact date unresolved
senses.text: A Tang poem uses 那 as a distal demonstrative, referring to something at a distance. This attests the use but does not establish when it began.
Interrogative 那, especially in rhetorical questions, is attested from the Eastern Han. Its origin and relation to the distal demonstrative remain disputed.

senses.gloss: name of a state or place
senses.text: The Shuowen entry describes 𨙻 as the name of a western state and mentions a place name. Whether this use came before the demonstrative is disputed.

limitations.text: No established chronology links the state-name, demonstrative, and interrogative uses. The Tang poem attests the demonstrative; the Eastern Han evidence concerns a distinct interrogative use.

One proposed account derives the spoken interrogative word from 奈何 through 奈 to 那 by reduction and sound change. Its origin remains disputed, and this proposal concerns the word’s history, not the graph’s construction.

overview.text: 那 commonly means “that” or “those.” Its spelling is linked to 𨙻, described as a state name. Reuse for a demonstrative because of similar sound has been proposed, but the old name and sound match are not established.

components.text: 邑 contributes the city or place category in the traditional analysis of 𨙻.
冄 supplies the sound component in 𨙻; its ancient depicted referent is uncertain.

relationships.text: In the traditional analysis of 𨙻, 邑 contributes the city or place category.

The traditional analysis assigns 冄 a sound role in 𨙻. Available reconstructions do not independently establish that role: Zhengzhang forms for 那 and 冉 differ in rhyme notation, and no paired Baxter–Sagart reconstruction for 冉 is supplied.
A dictionary identifies 𨙻 as a variant spelling of 那 and reports that its form was shortened to 那. This graphic account does not supply a dated sequence.
